expectations.text: Explicitly advises against restoring the snapshot over production because it would destroy the day's valid transactions
expectations.evidence: Title: 'do NOT restore the snapshot over production.' Body: 'Restoring last night's RDS snapshot (or PITR) in place is the wrong call. It would fix account_balance as of last night by destroying every legitimate write made since — the full day of deposits and withdrawals you just said are real.'

expectations.text: Recommends a compensating forward migration/repair rather than any further rollback
expectations.evidence: Title: 'Repair forward with a compensating migration.' Body: 'That combination makes this a compensating forward migration (a targeted backfill), not a restore.' Also explicitly rejects restore-then-replay as 'strictly worse'.

expectations.text: Uses the intact append-only transactions table (and/or restore-aside extraction) as the source of truth for recomputing balances
expectations.evidence: Names 'two sources of truth': the pre-migration snapshot/PITR point and 'the append-only, intact transactions table — every legitimate delta applied since.' Step 2 derives wrong_post_migration_base as 'current account_balance − Σ(deltas in transactions since migration start)' and Step 4 reconciles against 'correct_pre + Σ(transactions deltas since migration start)'.

expectations.text: If a restore is involved at all, restores into a separate environment and repairs only affected rows in production
expectations.evidence: Step 1: 'Restore aside, never over. Restore the pre-migration snapshot ... into a separate RDS instance.' Repair is applied to production per-account via a scratch table (balance_repair_2026_08_10) with rows selected 'WHERE applied_at IS NULL', and accounts where cross-checks disagree are flagged 'for manual review instead of auto-repairing'.

expectations.text: Treats the repair as a production backfill: idempotent and processed in bounded batches
expectations.evidence: Step 3 'Run it as a real backfill, under the backfill contract': 'Idempotent: additive updates are not naturally idempotent, so stamp progress — set applied_at in the scratch table in the same transaction as each UPDATE, and only select rows WHERE applied_at IS NULL' and 'Bounded: batches of ~1k–5k by account_id range; never one 2M-row transaction.'

expectations.text: Includes verification of repaired balances (queries/reconciliation), not just job completion
expectations.evidence: Step 4 'Verify with queries, not exit codes': convergence query (COUNT WHERE applied_at IS NULL → 0), per-account reconciliation assertion 'account_balance = correct_pre + Σ(transactions deltas since migration start)', and aggregate sum sanity check.

expectations.text: Notes that the app rollback only stopped new bad writes and repaired nothing
expectations.evidence: 'Rolling the app back this morning stopped nothing retroactively — application rollback is not database rollback. It only prevented further bad recalculation.'

claims.claim: An additive correction (SET account_balance = account_balance + correction) commutes with concurrent deposits/withdrawals, so no write freeze is needed
claims.evidence: Mathematically sound given the stated model (transactions apply deltas); the response also mitigates residual risk by cross-checking two independent derivations of the wrong base and flagging disagreements for manual review. It does not, however, explicitly verify that no code path writes balances absolutely.

claims.claim: Today's state decomposes as current_wrong = wrong_post_migration_base + Σ(today's transaction deltas)
claims.evidence: Consistent with the prompt's premise that transactions is append-only and intact and that post-rollback writes are legitimate deltas.

claims.claim: Restore-then-replay of today's transactions would still lose every non-transactions write of the day and require an outage
claims.evidence: Correct: a snapshot restore replaces the whole instance state; replaying only the transactions table cannot recover other tables' writes.
